axes.model_access: No built-in model weights: AI pieces connect to providers (OpenAI and others) through credentials, and an AI SDK supports building agents inside flows; self-hosting keeps credentials on the user’s instance (2026-11-21).
axes.runtime: Open-source self-hosting plus official cloud: production self-hosting uses Docker Compose with PostgreSQL and Redis, while the single-machine hobby container uses PGLite and an in-memory queue (not upgradable to Enterprise). The repo has 25,150 stars and last pushed 2026-10-21 (2026-11-21).
axes.local_files: Self-hosted data stays in the user’s environment: the hobby container writes to `~/.activepieces`, production uses the user’s PostgreSQL/Redis, and piece credentials and execution data remain on the instance; cloud data is vendor-hosted (2026-11-21).
axes.background: A always-on self-hosted instance carries schedule and webhook triggers; production uses Redis queue workers across instances, human-in-the-loop supports delays and approvals, and flows ship with auto retries and versioning (2026-11-21).
axes.tools: The pieces ecosystem is the core: the official MCP page says one server URL covers 770+ apps, while the README lists 280+ pieces available as MCP (both counts grow with releases). The builder includes loops, branches, auto retries, HTTP, Code with NPM, ASK AI, versioning and templates (2026-11-21).
axes.context: Step-to-step data passing and variable references are the main context; execution history persists per flow, and cross-flow sharing relies on explicit storage/queue pieces rather than implicit memory (2026-11-21).
axes.permissions: The community edition is MIT Expat, with enterprise features under the commercial `packages/ee` licence; SSO, projects and role controls sit on the ee line. MCP connections use OAuth2 with limited scopes, 256-bit encrypted credentials and no read-back API (2026-11-21).
axes.fit: Fit: self-hosted automation with an MIT core, hackable low-code and direct MCP exposure of pieces. Not fit: a Zapier-scale connector ecosystem or turnkey enterprise features (those sit on the ee commercial line) (2026-11-21).

runs: This entry checks the official install docs, repository README and MCP pages. Queue throughput, community-edition boundaries and specific piece availability need testing on one’s own instance.
